§9.6.6 Marks and Symbols in Cells

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-marks-and-symbols-in-cells · tables marks encoding

✅ Normative

A footnote marker MUST stay in the cell of the value it is attached to. An em-dash alone in a cell is a value and MUST be kept; a cell printed blank MUST stay blank. A cell whose content is a symbol or icon MUST be rendered as a bracketed transcription of what the mark asserts, and MUST NOT be replaced by an emoji.

A sun/water requirements table where the icons are the values — a full sun versus a partial sun, one droplet versus two. A rendering that leaves those cells empty says nothing at all.

| Subscribers¹ | 48,210³ |   ← superscripts attached to a value
| Dividend     | —       |   ← an em-dash standing alone in a cell
| Approved     | ✓       |   ← a checkmark standing in for a value

Footnote superscripts

  • A footnote marker MUST stay in the same cell as the value it is attached to, rendered with <sup>: 48,210<sup>3</sup>, New Program<sup>2</sup> — see Superscript and Subscript§7.2.11.
  • The marker MUST NOT be stripped, and MUST NOT be given a column of its own. It points at one number; separated from that number it points at nothing.

The em-dash

  • An em-dash alone in a cell is a value and MUST be rendered as —. In accounting it means zero, and we checked — a different claim from an empty cell, which means nothing here.
  • The rule holds in both directions, and the second is the one most often broken: a cell printed blank MUST be rendered as an empty cell, and a dash MUST NOT be supplied for it, however many of its neighbours carry one (never invent).

The same reasoning makes the structural blank meaningful in Triangles and Matrix Tables§9.8.2 and the coloured fill meaningful in Color as the Value§9.6.4 — a non-value that is a value.

Checkmarks, crosses and icons

  • A mark that stands in for a value MUST be rendered as a bracketed word stating what it asserts: [yes], [no], [checked], [locked], [icon: present].
  • The nearest emoji MUST NOT be substituted. An emoji looks faithful and is not: it carries a shape rather than the claim the page makes, and no two producers pick the same one.
  • Where a symbol is glued to a value rather than standing in for one — ▲ 512.40, a bare + or - carrying a superscript — the glyph MUST stay with the value in the cell, as printed. See Iconography and Symbols§7.3.4 for marks outside tables.
| Feature | Basic | Pro |
| SSO     | 🔒    | ✓   |   → | SSO | [locked] | [yes] |

A repeated mark is a scale

Some columns grade a value by printing the mark more than once — one droplet for low water, two for high; one star, three stars.

  • A repeated mark MUST be transcribed once per printed mark: [water], [water][water]. The count is the value; collapsing the pair to one token loses the distinction the column exists to draw.
  • A count notation such as [water:2] MUST NOT be used.
  • The vocabulary MUST distinguish every distinct mark the scale prints. A sun column printing a solid, a half-filled and an outline glyph is a three-step scale; a rendering with two names for it has lost a step.
